doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Elvis Costello commission idea
summary: He hopes to commission Elvis Costello, who writes for the Brodsky Quartet.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. In fact if people ask me now, I did an interview with the Jazz Times recently and they said, “what would you call yourself?” I guess the thing that I would call myself is an interpreter of songs, or an interpreter of material. That’s what I would call myself. I just try to filter my own personality into whatever music interests me, and that might be anything. In fact I’m trying to get in touch with Elvis Costello right now because I’ve got a middle person who works with him, to try to see if I can commission him to write something for me. He’s doing these classical things now, these chamber works.
I didn’t hear about that, wow.
Yeah. He’s been writing pieces for the Brodsky Quartet, the string quartet and that would be kind of interesting if I could get that.
